payload.headline: Tesla slips below a key zone as margins and cash flow keep shrinking

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have stalled, and its margins and cash flow are falling, but the stock is still priced near the top of its own 5-year valuation range and far above every cash-flow value.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: no trade while the price sits between support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 380.15–389.95.
summary.act_at: Revisit long-term near 293.94; no swing trade until a close above 389.95 or below 364.02

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 379.74, down 2.69% on the day. That puts it just under the 380.15–389.95 zone, the price area that buyers and sellers have fought over most (10 touches). Tesla opened Cybercab pre-orders for personal use with a $299 monthly fee, and a €3B Berlin Gigafactory expansion for the Cybercab was reported. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The numbers that change the business are getting worse. Revenue in the latest quarter was down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings show inventory up 15% while quarterly sales were up 0%, which can force price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. Some things are not at risk. Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash, so funding the €3B Berlin expansion (reported) is not a solvency question. The Cybercab pre-orders and Mercedes-Benz's new city driving assist (reported) matter for the self-driving story and competition, but neither shows up in revenue yet. The Tesla–SpaceX merger talk is speculative and is a governance and sentiment story, not a business one.

worth.text: At 379.74, Tesla is valued at a market cap of 1501.0B. That is 14.5 times sales and 417.9 times trailing earnings. The data says this price needs about 52% a year growth, while Tesla delivered 3% a year over 3 years. A cash-flow model (DCF) that discounts future free cash flow at about 10% gives 20.09 / 24.79 / 44.69 per share across bear, base and bull. Even with 30% starting growth, it gives only 44.29. If operating margin falls to 1%, the value drops to 21.41. The second method asks what the stock would cost at its usual price-to-sales range over the last 5 years. It gives 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81, and the current multiple sits at the 77th percentile of that history. The huge gap between the two methods comes from one question: do investors keep paying for future hopes such as autonomy and robotaxis, or do they start paying for today's cash flow? The fair-value range below assumes the first, which makes it the generous view.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range instead of on current free cash flow.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B gives Tesla room to fund the Cybercab and Berlin plans without stress.
Trailing revenue still rose to 103.6B from 95.6B, and quarterly growth was 15.78% just two quarters ago.
The Cybercab personal-use pre-orders at a $299 monthly fee point to a possible recurring revenue stream beyond car sales.
bear: Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B.
At 417.9 times trailing earnings, the price needs about 52% a year growth against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.
Inventory rose 15% while quarterly sales rose 0%, which raises the risk of price cuts that squeeze margins further.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the top of the own-history range and many times every cash-flow value (24.79 base).
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the generous method calls the stock expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. At this level the stock no longer needs a top-of-range multiple, so it earns a fresh look if margins stop falling.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled while margins and cash flow are falling, and the price still needs a top-of-history multiple. The business is graded D and the rules committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The trend is a flat range, and all three moving averages (375.25 to 385.94) are flat. The price sits between support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 380.15–389.95, and both zones are close compared with the 16.56 average daily move, so a stop would sit inside normal noise. A close above 389.95 or below 364.02 would show a direction.

decision.timing: Options price a 14.7% move by the 2027-01-15 expiry, before the 2027-01-27 report. That report is the next real test of margins and cash flow, and the Cybercab and merger headlines do not change that timing.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly revenue growth heading back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago.
The price falls to around 293.94, the middle of the own-history range, while operating margin holds at 3.35% or better.
Trailing free cash flow recovers from 3.3B back toward 6.8B, which would narrow the gap to the cash-flow values.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid. The close at 379.74 broke below the 380.15–389.95 zone, which confirmed that buyers are not defending the stock near the top of its valuation range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
